questions.question: Who developed the basic architecture of computer?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: C) John Von Neumann.**

The stored-program computer architecture is associated with John von Neumann and colleagues.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.1, Q1(i)

questions.question: Which of the following computer memory is fastest?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: A) Register.**

CPU registers are inside the processor and are faster than RAM or disk.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.1, Q1(ii)

questions.question: Computer address bus is:
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: C) Unidirectional.**

The CPU drives addresses onto the address bus, so it is conventionally unidirectional.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.1, Q1(iii)

questions.question: The address in the main memory is known as:
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: B) Physical address.**

A main-memory location is addressed by its physical address; a logical address is generated by the CPU before translation.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.1, Q1(iv)

questions.question: Which of the following registers can interact with secondary storage?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: C) MDR.**

The Memory Data Register holds data moving to/from memory and the I/O path; among the printed registers it is the expected answer.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.1, Q1(v)

questions.question: The status bit is also called as:
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: C) Flag bit.**

Condition/status bits are flag bits in the status register.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.1, Q1(vi)

questions.question: CISC stands for:
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: A) Complex Instruction Set Computer.**

CISC expands to Complex Instruction Set Computer.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.2, Q1(vii)

questions.question: In which of the following terms is the performance of cache memory measured?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: B) Hit ratio.**

Cache performance is commonly expressed by the hit ratio (hits divided by total accesses).
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.2, Q1(viii)

questions.question: Individual control words of the micro routine are called as:
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: B) Microinstruction.**

A microinstruction is one control word in a microprogram/micro routine.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.2, Q1(ix)

questions.question: Which circuit identifies the actual instruction when it was taken from the Instruction Register?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: C) Decoder.**

An instruction decoder interprets the opcode and generates control signals.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.2, Q1(x)

questions.question: The situation wherein the data of operands are not available is called:
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: A) Data hazard.**

A data hazard occurs when an instruction needs an operand that a previous instruction has not yet produced.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.2, Q1(xi)

questions.question: What will be the result after executing the instruction `ADD R1,#5245`? (The content of R1 is 2345.)
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: B) 758A.**

If the printed values are hexadecimal, `0x2345 + 0x5245 = 0x758A`, which matches option B. If read as decimal, the sum is 7590, option A; the hex-like options make B the intended answer.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.2, Q1(xii)

questions.question: In order to read multiple bytes of a row at the same time, we make use of:
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: D) Latch.**

A latch/row buffer holds the selected row so consecutive column addresses can deliver multiple bytes without repeating the row access.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.2, Q1(xiii)

questions.question: Which of the following computer buses connects the CPU to a memory on the system board?
questions.answer:
**Correct answer: C) System bus.**

The system bus connects the CPU, memory, and major system components on the motherboard.

questions.question:
a) What is the key concept of Von-Neumann Architecture?
b) Write down the internal connection between memory and processor.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: What is the key concept of Von-Neumann Architecture?

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write down the internal connection between memory and processor.

questions.answer:
**a)** The stored-program concept: instructions and data share one memory and are fetched/executed sequentially under control of the program counter.

**b)** The CPU connects to memory through the address bus, data bus, and control bus. MAR holds the address, MDR buffers data, and control lines signal read/write; the system bus ties these to main memory.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q2

questions.question:
a) Define addressing modes.
b) Describe various addressing modes of 8086 microprocessor with examples.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Describe various addressing modes of 8086 microprocessor with examples.

questions.answer:
**a)** Addressing modes specify how the effective address of an operand is derived from instruction fields and registers.

**b)** 8086 modes include immediate (`MOV AX, 5`), register (`MOV AX, BX`), direct (`MOV AX, [1234H]`), register indirect (`MOV AX, [BX]`), based/indexed (`MOV AX, [BX+SI]`), based indexed with displacement (`MOV AX, [BX+SI+4]`), and relative/branch addressing.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q3

questions.question:
a) What is pipelining?
b) Write down the differences between RISC and CISC.
c) Explain different pipeline hazards.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write down the differences between RISC and CISC.

questions.answer:
**a)** Pipelining overlaps instruction fetch, decode, execute, memory access, and write-back stages so several instructions are in progress simultaneously.

**b)** RISC uses a small, simple, fixed-length instruction set, load/store architecture, and hardwired control; CISC uses complex variable-length instructions, many addressing modes, and often microprogrammed control.

**c)** Structural hazards occur when hardware resources conflict; data hazards occur when operands are not yet available; control hazards occur when branches change the instruction flow.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q4

questions.question:
a) Explain the function of BIU and EU of 8086 microprocessor.
b) Explain maximum and minimum modes of 8086 microprocessor.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Explain the function of BIU and EU of 8086 microprocessor.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Explain maximum and minimum modes of 8086 microprocessor.

questions.answer:
**a)** The Bus Interface Unit fetches instructions into the queue, computes physical addresses using segment registers, and handles bus cycles; the Execution Unit decodes and executes instructions using the ALU and registers.

**b)** In minimum mode, the 8086 generates all control signals itself for a single-processor system. In maximum mode, it uses a bus controller (8288) and supports multiprocessor/coprocessor configurations.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q5

questions.question:
a) Explain the direct mapping technique for cache memory organization.
b) What is virtual memory?

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Explain the direct mapping technique for cache memory organization.

questions.answer:
**a)** Each main-memory block maps to exactly one cache line, usually `line = block_number mod number_of_lines`. The tag stored in the line identifies which block is present; it is simple but can suffer conflict misses.

**b)** Virtual memory gives programs a large logical address space backed by secondary storage; an MMU maps virtual pages to physical frames and swaps pages on demand.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q6

questions.question:
a) Differentiate between fixed point representation and floating point representation.
b) Represent the IEEE standard for single and double floating point number.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Differentiate between fixed point representation and floating point representation.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Represent the IEEE standard for single and double floating point number.

questions.answer:
**a)** Fixed point has an implied fixed radix position and a limited range; floating point stores sign, exponent, and significand, trading precision for a much wider dynamic range.

**b)** IEEE 754 single precision: 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias 127), 23 fraction bits. Double precision: 1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits (bias 1023), 52 fraction bits. Normal value: `(-1)^s × 1.fraction × 2^(exponent−bias)`.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q7

questions.question:
a) What do you mean by Arithmetic Shift Right (ASR)?
b) Multiply (−11) and (−9) using Booth's Algorithm.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: What do you mean by Arithmetic Shift Right (ASR)?

questions.answer:
**a)** ASR shifts bits right and replicates the sign bit in the most significant position, preserving the sign of a two's-complement number; it approximates division by two with rounding toward negative infinity.

**b)** Use 5-bit operands with a 6-bit accumulator: `M = −11 = 110101` (sign-extended), `−M = +11 = 001011`, `Q = −9 = 10111`, `Q₋₁ = 0`, `A = 000000`. On `Q₀Q₋₁ = 10` do `A = A − M`; on `01` do `A = A + M`; then arithmetic-shift `A,Q,Q₋₁` right.

| Step | Action before the shift | A | Q | Q₋₁ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| initial | — | 000000 | 10111 | 0 |
| 1 | `A = A + 11` | 001011 | 10111 | 0 |
| 1 after ASR | — | 000101 | 11011 | 1 |
| 2 | no add, ASR | 000010 | 11101 | 1 |
| 3 | no add, ASR | 000001 | 01110 | 1 |
| 4 | `A = A − 11` | 110110 | 01110 | 1 |
| 4 after ASR | — | 111011 | 00111 | 0 |
| 5 | `A = A + 11` | 000110 | 00111 | 0 |
| 5 after ASR | — | 000011 | 00011 | 1 |

The double-length product `A:Q = 0001100011` is `+99`.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q8
questions.sourceNote: The scan asks for a worked Booth multiplication; the model answer supplies the add/subtract and arithmetic-shift table. No official key was supplied.

questions.question:
a) What is instruction cycle?
b) Write down the functional block diagram of control memory.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write down the functional block diagram of control memory.

questions.answer:
**a)** An instruction cycle is the sequence of fetching an instruction, decoding it, fetching operands, executing it, accessing memory if needed, writing back the result, and handling interrupts before the next instruction.

**b)** A textual block diagram: Control Address Register → Control Memory (microprogram) → Control Buffer Register / microinstruction → decoding/next-address logic → control signals to CPU datapath; the sequencer feeds the next address back to the CAR.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q9
questions.sourceNote: The requested block diagram is described textually rather than attached as a separate image asset.

questions.question:
a) Write short notes on any two: (a) Flynn's Classification of Computer, (b) RISC pipelining, (c) Memory hierarchy, (d) TLB.
b) Answer any two of the four listed topics.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Write short notes on any two: (a) Flynn's Classification of Computer, (b) RISC pipelining, (c) Memory hierarchy, (d) TLB.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Answer any two of the four listed topics.

questions.answer:
**a)** Flynn's taxonomy classifies architectures by instruction/data streams: SISD, SIMD, MISD, MIMD. RISC pipelining uses simple uniform stages (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) with forwarding/branch handling to sustain near one instruction per cycle.

**b)** Memory hierarchy orders register → cache → main memory → secondary storage by speed, cost, and capacity. A TLB is a cache of recent virtual-to-physical page translations inside the MMU; a TLB hit avoids a page-table walk.
questions.sourcePage: Computer Science and Organization .pdf, p.3, Q10
questions.sourceNote: The question asks for any two short notes; the model answer supplies all four for completeness.
